comparator.name: Linguistics
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations and course catalogue specify 60 EC per year in the broad Linguistics route. The first-year language choice is illustrated by the four-course Czech sequence. The 30 EC of third-year free electives can be used for a minor, electives, a placement or study abroad, subject to the applicable conditions.
components: The year also includes a zero-credit Academic Literacy Test and tutoring. Tutoring continues in later years.
Complete Phonetics before this course. It follows in the next teaching block.
Czech is the example for the 24 EC Language X requirement. Students choose one language and complete four courses.
Requires completion of Czech Language Acquisition 1.
Requires completion of Czech Language Acquisition 2.
Requires completion of Czech Language Acquisition 3.

Requires a positive binding study advice, Introduction to Linguistics, and at least one of Phonology, Syntax, or Semantics and Pragmatics.

core: Speech sounds, word formation, grammar, semantics, pragmatics and cross-linguistic structure
Language acquisition, psycholinguistics, cognition, development, neurolinguistics and clinical language study
Language variation, sociolinguistics, multilingualism, interaction and communication in society
Experimental and field research, statistics, language documentation and independent linguistic inquiry
adjacent: Written, spoken and multimodal discourse, rhetoric, literary interpretation and media communication
Speech processing, language data and computational language applications
questions: How do mind, society and media shape language use and meaning?

Introduces nervous systems, behaviour and comparative neurobiology, with laboratory and literature-based work.

provides concepts for analysing social interaction, institutions, identity, inequality and the social settings in which language varies
provides Python programming and computational problem-solving foundations for analysing language and speech data
examines sensory processing, perception and action as cognitive foundations relevant to speech perception and production
Studies cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan, using case studies and a life-story interview.
examines social cognition, persuasion, group influence and interpersonal processes that shape communication
Designs qualitative inquiries using interviews, ethnography, coding and thematic interpretation.
examines higher-order cognition, memory, executive control and decision processes that interact with language comprehension and use
analyses framing, persuasion and ethical communication in political, legal, media and institutional discourse
Designs and evaluates algorithms and data structures, including string matching and performance experiments.
develops regression, classification, clustering and model evaluation for detecting patterns in empirical language or speech datasets
Studies the neuroscience of language, including acquisition, bilingualism, comprehension, production, aphasia and dyslexia. Includes hands-on experimental approaches.
Synthesizes behavioural and health research through systematic review, effect sizes and meta-analysis in R.
examines voice, performance, poetry and multimodal communication through critical and creative research
applies advanced theories of interpretation and meaning in an independent text-research project
Develops beginner Dutch through conversation, listening, functional writing and cultural study.
places major literary works and written expression in historical and cultural contexts
examines modernity, colonialism, identity and social theory as contexts for language variation and power
compares oral and literary traditions, cultural transmission and representations of power across languages and regions
introduces formal analysis of film and audiovisual media as systems of communication and meaning
examines how material media and technologies shape communication, knowledge circulation and cultural memory
analyses memoir, autobiography, diary and travel narratives as socially situated uses of voice and identity
examines identity, conformity, marginalisation and social change through popular media narratives
Develops debate, storytelling and speaking through community-engaged teaching with primary-school children.
develops advanced analysis of how verbal narratives change through adaptation into audiovisual form
studies how media representation constructs or resists racialised identities and power
analyses documentary representation across social, ethical and aesthetic contexts and develops multimodal production
Analyses how the climate crisis is framed and contested across texts, film, protest art and social media, then develops a communication project.

alternatives.label: Language, cognition & communication research
alternatives.concept: Study how people acquire, understand and produce language. Combine psycholinguistics and the study of the brain with stylistic analysis, experimental design, statistics and computational methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines psycholinguistics and cognition with experimental research, statistics, data science, programming, algorithms, rhetoric and textual meaning. The label describes that related-fields centre and avoids claiming a full Linguistics programme.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics and later cognition courses. Introductory research and statistics precede advanced methods. Programming precedes algorithms.

alternatives.label: Language, discourse & media in society
alternatives.concept: Study how language conveys meaning and shapes social life. Combine stylistics, rhetoric, introductory Dutch and sociology with literary interpretation, film and public communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on social language use, rhetoric, stylistics, psycholinguistics, literature and media. Its label states discourse and media as the organising fields rather than presenting it as formal Linguistics.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics. Introductory sociology, literature and rhetoric precede advanced social theory, literary analysis and persuasion. Media foundations prepare for applied discourse analysis and documentary work.
alternatives.distinctness: 13 courses (97.5 EC) differ in each direction. The cognition option emphasizes experimental design, statistics and computing. The discourse option develops language learning, literary interpretation, media analysis and public rhetoric.

candidates.label: Language, discourse and media in society
Formal linguistic structure and cross-linguistic comparison

selection.assessment: Two coherent options study language through cognition and empirical methods or through discourse, literature and media. A formal linguistics option would need sustained study of phonetics, morphology, phonology, syntax and cross-linguistic analysis. General programming, algorithms and model evaluation offer foundations for analysing data but do not provide a language technology sequence.

blocks: Formal linguistics, speech and language acquisition
Both analyse how linguistic form creates meaning; UCR provides stylistics and literary linguistics rather than a full semantics-and-pragmatics course.
Both develop beginning proficiency in a modern language. UCR teaches Dutch in one course. UvA’s Czech example is a four-course sequence.
UCR has no introductory linguistics survey covering the comparator’s formal subfields and scientific methods.
UCR has no dedicated phonetics course.
UCR has no transcription course or practical phonetic-transcription sequence.
UCR has no dedicated morphology course.
UCR has no dedicated sociolinguistics course; sociology and communication courses provide related perspectives only.
UCR has no second course in the comparator’s selected Czech sequence.
UCR has no third course in the comparator’s selected Czech sequence.
UCR has no fourth course in the comparator’s selected Czech sequence.
UCR has no dedicated phonology course.
UCR has no dedicated syntax course.
UCR has no cumulative linguistic-theory course following formal linguistics prerequisites.
Both examine language comprehension and production. UCR also studies the neural basis of language, acquisition, bilingualism and language impairments.
Both examine cognition and mental representation; UCR is a general Philosophy of Mind course rather than a language-and-cognition humanities seminar.
UCR Psycholinguistics discusses acquisition and bilingualism but does not reproduce a dedicated second-language-acquisition course.
UCR has no clinical-linguistics course or clinical language assessment practice.
Research methods, data and language technology
Both develop research design and empirical inquiry; UCR provides a general methods-and-statistics foundation rather than a linguistics-specific first-year project.
Both develop experimental design and statistical analysis; UCR teaches these in psychology rather than as linguistics-specific methods.
UCR offers general data science, machine learning and algorithms but no dedicated speech-processing course.
UCR has no formal Linguistics specialization module or field-linguistics equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
The compulsory Linguistics thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.

notes.text: The UCR options share interests in language acquisition, comprehension, style and communication. UvA adds sustained training in phonetics, transcription, morphology, phonology, syntax, clinical linguistics and speech processing, with a staged research sequence and an independent thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Linguistics at the University of Amsterdam studies how languages are structured, acquired, processed and used. Students learn a modern language, analyse speech and meaning, and complete an independent research thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers two related options. One studies language and cognition with experimental and computational methods. The other studies discourse, literature and media. UvA provides a deeper sequence in linguistic structure, analysis of speech and language research.
